According to arXiv 2404.13060, it is insufficient to audit only the final AI product because AI systems, particularly black-box models, pose risks that change over time, and issues such as training data attacks can be imperceptible in the final model. Therefore, evaluating inputs and processes is necessary, as the entire design process must be overseen, similar to industries like pharmaceuticals and nuclear power. The document emphasizes that an AI system is not a single static artifact that can be evaluated in isolation; it involves complex relationships between individual changes and ethical and safety concerns.

The additional processes recommended include auditing the entire process from data collection and training through to post-deployment monitoring. This involves ongoing checks and revisions of practices and norms, addressing both current and anticipated risks, and ensuring that audits are not merely point-in-time evaluations but involve continuous risk analysis and engagement with diverse stakeholders.
